status.headline: FAA is gradually lifting the ground stop
status.detail: The FAA says it is gradually lifting restrictions and resuming normal operations as systems come back online, with some flights already cleared to depart. An airline source says the FAA has traced the outage to a problem with network routers. More than 10,200 flights are delayed and over 4,000 canceled, and delays will run well past the restart.

items.source: NBC News live updates and ABC News, flight-tracking data
items.summary: NBC News, citing a flight-tracking site, puts Friday's US delays above 10,200 and cancellations above 4,000. That is roughly ten times the cancellation count from mid-afternoon. The totals will keep rising as airlines unwind the backlog after the restart.
items.title: Delays pass 10,200 with more than 4,000 cancellations

items.source: FAA, via Fox News live updates. Time is approximate.
items.title: FAA says it is gradually lifting restrictions as systems come back online
items.summary: The FAA says it has been gradually lifting restrictions and resuming normal air traffic operations as its systems recover. It warns that delays and cancellations will linger nationwide. This is the first official word that the stop is ending, and it supersedes the earlier unconfirmed lift reports.
echoes: CNBC headline: stop lifted after four hours

items.source: CNN, citing an airline source; details relayed by Clash Report. Time is approximate.
items.title: FAA tells airlines a network router problem caused the outage
items.summary: CNN reports the FAA told airlines the nationwide outage came from a problem with network routers. A secondary outlet relaying CNN and CBS says the fault is believed to have started at Chicago Midway, on a radio network run by a contractor, after an update made it reboot and crash. The FAA has not said any of this on the record.

items.source: FAA alert, via ABC News and Fox News live updates. Time is approximate.
items.title: FAA lets some flights depart while the stop stays in effect
items.summary: Before the wider easing, the FAA said in an alert that some flights were being allowed to depart as en route facilities recovered. Early clearances included overseas departures, among them flights to Germany and Prague. ABC's file at that point still described the ground stop as in effect.

items.source: Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines statement, via CNN. Time is approximate.
items.title: Flights within Alaska and Hawaii can still depart, airlines say
items.summary: Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines say flights within Alaska and within Hawaii are still able to depart. The carriers have canceled some flights and diverted others because of the stop. They warn it will take time for operations to recover once it is lifted.
echoes: ABC News: Boston Logan transatlantic departures

items.source: Associated Press, republished by WRAL; TheStreet. Time is approximate.
items.title: Ground stop now runs through at least 11 pm ET Friday
items.summary: The Associated Press reports the nationwide stop order now runs through at least 11 pm Eastern on Friday. TheStreet noted earlier that flights would be held at their origins past the original 5 pm advisory window. No official restart time has been announced, and nothing says departures will resume at 11 pm.

items.source: Associated Press, republished by WRAL. Time is approximate.
items.title: Former United pilot ties the outage to aging air traffic control technology
items.summary: Former United Airlines pilot Steve Arroyo told AP the failure resembles the regional outage that disrupted hundreds of Northeast flights in September, only on a national scale. He linked both episodes to outdated air traffic control technology. This is outside analysis rather than a finding, since the FAA has not identified what failed.

items.source: Associated Press, republished by WRAL. Time is approximate.
items.title: American passengers in Wichita sent back to the gate after an hour on the runway
items.summary: Travelers on an American Airlines flight from Wichita to Chicago first got texts blaming air traffic conditions in Chicago. After roughly an hour on the runway, the captain told them the problem was nationwide and the plane taxied back to the gate. Passengers got off, and the airline said nobody would be rebooked for at least an hour.

items.source: NBC News, MS NOW. Time is approximate.
items.title: Senior lawmakers say they have not been briefed on the cause
items.summary: A Republican leadership aide told NBC News that senior members had not received a briefing from the administration as of early evening. The top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee said he has not been told the cause either. Pressure for an explanation is now coming from both parties.

items.source: NBC News live updates. Time is approximate.
items.title: Some airports are running out of room to park aircraft
items.summary: NBC News reports that some airports are starting to run short of space as arrivals keep landing while nothing departs. An aviation safety expert said planes may have to be moved and parked on taxiways. This is the main physical constraint that gets worse the longer the stop lasts.

items.source: FAA advisory, via FOX 4 Dallas-Fort Worth. Time is approximate.
items.summary: An FAA advisory extended flight plan drop times to 240 minutes at every en route center. The advisory blamed a nationwide communications failure for the change. FOX 4 did not say when the advisory was issued, and no restart time came with it.
items.title: FAA extends flight plan drop times to 240 minutes at all en route centers

items.source: Fes News Media headline, via search. Time is approximate.
items.summary: A news site headline says the telecom outage hit 22 air traffic control centers. Only the headline was visible in search results, and the page text could not be retrieved, so the count rests on one source. It differs in scope from the FAA's wording about multiple centers and Duffy's about all centers, which have not been reconciled.
items.title: News site headline puts the telecom outage at 22 control centers

items.source: American Airlines and Delta statements, via Newsweek, AP and WCVB. Time is approximate.
items.title: American expects disruption all day; Delta confirms it is affected
items.summary: American Airlines says departures are paused nationwide and that it expects schedule disruption for the rest of the day, depending on how long the stop lasts. It says all staff will work to move customers once the FAA lifts the order. Delta has also confirmed its flights are affected, and United says the FAA is handling international departures one by one.

items.source: Delta and United waivers, via ABC News live updates. Time is approximate.
items.title: Delta and United waive change fees for travelers hit by the stop
items.summary: Delta is waiving change fees for travel on Friday and Saturday. United is waiving both change fees and fare differences for rebooked trips originally set between November 12 and November 20. The waivers give stranded and delayed passengers a way to move plans without extra cost as cancellations climb.

items.source: NBC News (Jeff Guzzetti), Associated Press. Time is approximate.
items.title: Safety experts call the outage extraordinary and unexplained
items.summary: A former accident investigator told NBC News the outage is extraordinary and that he cannot say what would cause it. An expert quoted by AP said this differs from 9/11 because aircraft were not ordered to land and pilots could likely still reach controllers at airports. AP's running file is the wire source most local outlets are republishing.

items.source: CBS News law enforcement sources, relayed by Latin Times. Time is approximate.
items.title: Sources point to radio frequencies used by pilots and controllers
items.summary: One law enforcement source told CBS News the problem involves radio frequencies and how pilots communicate. A second source said TSA is still trying to pin down exactly where it began. This lines up with the early frequency-outage notices but is not an official finding.

items.source: Contractor, via ABC News live updates. Time is approximate.
items.title: Contractor says the FAA's new AI program did not cause the stop
items.summary: A contractor told ABC News that a new artificial intelligence program was not behind the nationwide ground stop. The statement speaks to earlier speculation about the FAA's recently deployed AI congestion tool. ABC's update gives no further detail on what the contractor built or how it ruled the program out.

items.source: DHS Secretary Mullin at the White House, via The Hill, NBC News, CBS News and Fox Business. Time is approximate.
items.title: Trump has been briefed; Mullin says this is not 9/11
items.summary: Speaking outside the White House, the Homeland Security Secretary said the president has been briefed and that Duffy spoke with him about the outage. He said the stop is unlike the one after 9/11 and that the public has no reason to be afraid, while conceding that a nationwide stoppage amounts to a crisis. He added that it is too early to say how long it will last.
echoes: AP: Mullin says president was briefed

items.source: FAA statement and X post, via CNN and HuffPost. Time is approximate.
items.summary: About an hour after Duffy's post, the FAA attributed the stop to a temporary telecommunications outage and said flights were halted out of caution. The agency says every flight has been accounted for. It still has not said what failed inside the telecom system or when departures restart.
items.title: FAA names a temporary telecommunications outage as the cause

items.source: HuffPost, ABC7 Chicago live updates. Time is approximate.
items.summary: A House member said on cable news that the administration needs to explain what happened quickly given how many travelers are stranded. Coverage is also resurfacing Duffy's request for another 30 billion dollars to finish the air traffic control overhaul, which the White House is lobbying Congress to approve. Expect the outage to be used on both sides of that funding argument.
items.title: Lawmakers start pressing DOT and the White House for answers

items.source: Passenger videos compiled by TMZ; CNN airport reports. Time is approximate.
items.summary: Clips circulating from inside aircraft include an Atlanta pilot telling a Tampa-bound cabin the stop could last up to seven hours. Another passenger reported luggage being unloaded despite expecting a two-hour delay, and a reality TV personality posted that she was frightened. CNN crews at O'Hare and Newark said some travelers in the terminals did not yet know about the stop.
items.title: Passenger videos: pilots warn of hours-long waits, bags pulled off planes

items.source: Airlive, AirNav Radar data
items.summary: An aviation news site says control centers are clearing airspace of new departures and preparing for ATC Zero, the status for a facility that cannot provide normal separation. It also cites tracking data showing about 3,115 aircraft still en route to US airports. No official source has used the term ATC Zero, so treat it as a single-source claim.
items.title: Trade site claims centers are preparing for ATC Zero

items.source: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to reporters, via ABC News, CNN and TMZ
items.summary: The Homeland Security Secretary told reporters there is no indication yet of a hostile act and described it as a telecommunications outage for now. He said it is unrelated to Thursday's global Microsoft outage but declined to rule out any cause, a cyberattack included. He also said communications were overwhelmed at some levels without going fully dark, and that no restart time has been set.
items.title: DHS: no sign of an attack so far, and no timeline to resume
echoes: AP: Mullin sees no indication of attack

items.source: The National Herald; disputed by Clash Report and others. Time is approximate: neither report carried a timestamp.
items.summary: At least one outlet says the FAA has begun lifting restrictions and flights are gradually resuming, with lingering delays around New York and Boston. Other coverage says accounts claiming a lift have no official confirmation. Until the FAA or DOT says so, this tracker keeps the status as in effect.
items.title: Conflicting reports on whether the stop is being lifted

items.source: CNN live updates, citing law enforcement sources
items.summary: CNN reports that early indications from law enforcement sources point away from a cyberattack. This is a preliminary assessment and no agency has said it on the record. The FAA still has not named a root cause.
items.title: Preliminary read from law enforcement sources: not a cyberattack

items.source: Gizmodo, Clash Report
items.summary: The FAA's public alert site has been loading only intermittently. At one point its status board did not show the national stop, which fed claims that it had ended. The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey is sending all questions to the FAA and could not say whether JFK departures were moving.
items.title: FAA status site is flaky and briefly did not list the national stop

items.source: Axios
items.summary: Axios points out that the FAA has been rolling out an AI tool for managing airspace congestion. It says there is no indication yet that the tool is connected to today's communications failure. Treat this as context that people are already speculating about, not as a cause.
items.title: Axios notes the FAA's new AI congestion tool, with no known link

items.source: CNBC, Paddle Your Own Kanoo
items.summary: United says airborne flights continue and no new domestic flights will leave while the stop stands. An internal Alaska Airlines message seen by CNBC attributes the problem to communications and radar issues. Trade coverage warns that crew duty limits and out-of-position aircraft will push cancellations into the weekend even after a lift.
items.title: United holds domestic departures; Alaska memo cites comms and radar

items.source: FOX 5 Atlanta, FlightAware data
items.summary: Hartsfield-Jackson is letting arrivals land while departures are suspended. FlightAware counts were at 521 delays and 22 cancellations for the airport as of the report. The FAA has given the airport no estimate for when technicians will fix the problem.
items.title: Atlanta logs 521 delays and 22 cancellations so far

items.source: Yahoo News reporter aboard a United flight at LAX
items.summary: A reporter held on the tarmac at LAX relayed her pilot's announcement that the stop is expected to last until 11 pm ET. The pilot said the communications outage started at Kansas City Center and spread nationwide. That origin matches one trade outlet's account but has no official confirmation.
items.title: Pilot tells passengers the outage began at Kansas City Center

items.source: FAA statement, via CNBC, Axios and Reuters
items.summary: The agency's own statement describes communication issues at multiple control centers, where Duffy said all of them. A separate FAA line refers to a technical issue with telecommunications at many facilities. The gap between multiple and all has not been reconciled.
items.title: FAA statement says multiple centers, a narrower scope than Duffy's

items.source: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on X
items.summary: The Transportation Secretary confirmed the stop at 4:16 pm ET and tied it to a communication issue affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. He said FAA technicians are investigating and promised updates. He gave no cause and no time for departures to resume.
items.title: Duffy: communication issue hit all en route control centers

items.source: X: Anna Giaritelli (Washington Examiner), via Clash Report
items.summary: A Washington Examiner reporter shared notices describing a stop for all centers and all destinations because of widespread frequency outages. She quoted an unnamed FAA source calling the situation unheard of. Radio chatter circulating alongside it had Delta and United crews in Boston reporting frequency problems just before the national order.
items.title: Reporter posts notices citing widespread frequency outages

items.source: FAA Air Traffic Control System Command Center
items.summary: The advisory took effect at 3:54 pm ET and cites extraordinary circumstances and safety. All departures hold until further notice, airborne flights continue to their destinations, and inbound international flights are handled one by one. It is the first nationwide stop since the January 2023 NOTAM failure and the second since 9/11.
items.title: Command Center orders every US airport ground stopped

items.source: X: @theATCapp and replies
items.summary: An aviation account posted that controllers and pilots around the country were reporting a nationwide ground stop, minutes ahead of the official advisory. A follow-up said Canadian ATC attributed it to an FAA radio outage. Replies included a passenger stuck on the ground at LAX whose pilot confirmed the stop.
items.title: Controllers and pilots flag a nationwide stop on X before the FAA does

items.source: FAA advisories, via CBS News and ABC News
items.summary: Before the national order, the FAA stopped traffic at both Chicago airports and cited an equipment outage with comms problems. Those two stops turned out to be the leading edge of a wider failure. The local advisories dropped off the FAA board once the national stop replaced them.
items.title: O'Hare and Midway ground stopped first over an equipment outage

topics.label: Speculation about the FAA's new AI tool
topics.summary: Axios flagged the FAA's new AI congestion tool, and a contractor has since told ABC News the program was not behind the stop.

topics.label: ATC modernization money and blame
topics.summary: Lawmakers want an explanation from DOT and the White House. Coverage is tying the outage to the pending 30 billion dollar request for the control system overhaul.

topics.label: Was it an attack?
topics.summary: DHS says there is no sign of a hostile act so far and that it is unrelated to Thursday's Microsoft outage. CBS and ABC headlines say the White House sees no indication of a nefarious act, though nothing has been ruled out.

topics.label: Did it start at Kansas City Center?
topics.summary: A pilot announcement and one trade outlet place the first failure at Kansas City Center before it spread. No official has confirmed that.

topics.label: Early claims that the stop was lifted
topics.summary: Some accounts and at least one outlet said restrictions were easing. Nothing official supports that, and the FAA status site has been loading intermittently.

topics.label: Refunds, waivers and airline stocks
topics.summary: Delta and United have issued change-fee waivers, and consumer outlets are explaining what refunds travelers are owed for canceled flights.

topics.label: When do flights restart?
topics.summary: The FAA says it is gradually lifting restrictions and some flights are already departing. No time has been given for a full return to normal.

topics.label: Stuck on planes and in terminals
topics.summary: Passenger videos show cabins held at gates and on taxiways, bags being pulled, and travelers who had not heard about the stop.

topics.label: Cancellations and the weekend knock-on
topics.summary: Delays are above 10,200 with more than 4,000 cancellations. Crew duty limits and out-of-position aircraft are expected to push disruption into the weekend.

topics.label: What actually failed at the FAA?
topics.summary: The FAA calls it a temporary telecommunications outage. An airline source says the FAA has traced it to network routers, but the agency has not confirmed that on the record.
